Why training should be your culture

Without it, people feel lost

“Without proper training, small businesses can struggle. Employees might feel lost, they feel there's no long-term career for them, productivity can drop, and the business can suffer.”

Auditors ask your staff, not you

Assessors from BSI, NQA and LRQA will ask the people doing the work what they do and why. Awareness training is what lets them answer in their own words.

You stop buying in every audit

Internal auditor training gives you someone in house who can run the audit cycle with confidence, rather than commissioning it each time it comes round.

Questions

Training questions we get asked

Where we don't yet have a published answer, we say so rather than guess.

Do you deliver training at our premises?

We have done. David delivered AS9100 training to AT Engineering at their own site, ahead of their NQA assessment. Ask when you call and we'll confirm what works for your team — we schedule consultancy visits around your operations, and training is no different.

Is there an AS9100 course in the catalogue?

Not as a listed course, but we have delivered AS9100 training in practice, covering what the aerospace standard means for each member of staff. David is a BSI qualified AS9100 auditor. If you need it, say so.

What does a course cost, and how long does it take?

We would rather quote than publish a price list, because courses are built around your procedures and the size of the group. Ring us and we will scope it. There is no contract to sign.

Do you train our people, or do we have to send them somewhere?

We train your people. The whole point of internal auditor training is that the capability stays with you afterwards, so you can run your own audit cycle rather than buying it in each year.

Can training be part of a certification project?

Yes, and it usually is. Training is stage four of how we run a registration project, between building the system and running the first internal audits. If you are already a client, ask your consultant.
